candidates.excerpt: SEATTLE — It’s been three years since testing indicated a solution for “loss of shunt,” the connectivity issues that can prevent grade crossing warning devices from operating as a train approaches. But trains are still awaiting the equipment that solves the problem. Following tests conducted by Canadian National in conjunction with Amtrak, CN issued a report substantiating its belief that onboard shunt-enhancing antennas can reliably eliminate faulty track-circuit conductivity. However, installation of antennas on Midwest-owned Charger locomotives to address shunt issues on routes out of Chicago won’t occur until agreements between the states and Amtrak are completed. In the Pacific Northwest and California, the absence of those devices on Airo and Venture cab cars prevents those cars from leading trains. Carriers left the ETA blank in 42,832 cases, or 8.43% of shipments, most often while cargo was waiting at a transshipment port. The analysis was carried out while Tradlinx was building and validating AI-ETA, its arrival prediction model. Key findings • Carrier ETAs were missing for 8.43% of shipments. Across more than 500,000 shipments a year, carriers left the ETA blank in 42,832 cases. • Nearly three in four gaps occur at the transshipment port. The ETA for the intermediate transshipment port was missing in 30,929 cases (6.09%), the final-destination ETA of transshipment cargo in 6,168 cases (1.21%), and the destination ETA of direct shipments in 5,735 cases (1.13%). candidates.excerpt: Moody’s: life insurers increasingly rely on RNFs US life insurers are increasingly using rated note feeders (RNFs) to gain exposure to private credit markets, according to a report by Moody’s Ratings. Alongside the potential for diversification and enhanced yields, RNFs are seen as a capital efficient way of accessing private strategies such as direct lending, infrastructure, asset-based finance, and commercial real estate. Moody’s estimates that 35 per cent of US life insurance investments go towards private credit. Media and entertainment loans saw the next-largest markdowns, followed by consumer services, according to Cliffwater Direct Lending Index data cited by the asset manager.
